20solve%20those%20tasks%20or%20use%20those%20equations%20to%20generate%20the%20plots%20below.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20goal%20is%20not%20to%20memorize%20one%20%22correct%22%20muscle%20model.%20The%20goal%20is%20to%20connect%20the%20pieces%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20a%20neural%20control%20signal%20becomes%20muscle%20activation%3B%0A%20%20%20%202.%20activation%20scales%20active%20muscle%20force%3B%0A%20%20%20%203.%20active%20force%20changes%20with%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20and%20velocity%3B%0A%20%20%20%204.%20passive%20muscle%20and%20tendon%20elasticity%20change%20the%20force%20transmitted%20to%20the%20skeleton.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Before%20running%20the%20notebook%2C%20sketch%20what%20you%20expect%20from%20a%20muscle%20that%20receives%20a%20step%20command%3A%20does%20activation%20jump%20instantly%2C%20rise%20smoothly%2C%20overshoot%2C%20or%20decay%20slowly%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20existing%20interactive%20curves%20let%20you%20separate%20the%20active%2C%20passive%2C%20tendon%2C%20velocity%20and%20activation%20ingredients%20before%20combining%20them.%20Use%20normalized%20variables%20carefully%3A%20unit%20force%20means%20maximum%20isometric%20force%20at%20optimal%20length%2C%20not%20one%20newton.%20Make%20one%20parameter%20change%20at%20a%20time%20and%20compare%20with%20the%20equations.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Try%20the%20distributed%20**Exercises**%20before%20opening%20their%20collapsed%20worked%20solutions.%20Then%20use%20the%20**Checkpoint%20questions**%20and%20attempt%20the%20**Problems**%20independently%3B%20their%20panels%20contain%20final%20answers%20only.%20Predict%20the%20effect%20of%20a%20parameter%20change%20before%20running%20it%2C%20and%20check%20units%20and%20limiting%20cases.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Opening%20challenge.**%20If%20activation%20stays%20constant%2C%20must%20muscle%20force%20stay%20constant%20while%20the%20muscle%20shortens%3F%20Predict%20how%20length%2C%20velocity%20and%20tendon%20stretch%20affect%20the%20answer.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20dependency%20declaration%20at%20the%20top%20of%20this%20file%20lists%20the%20packages%20used%20by%20this%20guide.%20Marimo%20runs%20cells%20in%20dependency%20order.%20Run%20the%20notebook%20in%20an%20editor%20to%20use%20its%20displays%20and%20controls%3B%20the%20computational%20examples%20below%20explain%20their%20inputs%20before%20using%20them.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20There%20are%20two%20major%20classes%20of%20muscle%20models%20that%20have%20been%20used%20in%20biomechanics%20and%20motor%20control%3A%20the%20Hill-type%20and%20Huxley-type%20models.%20They%20differ%20mainly%20on%20how%20the%20contractile%20element%20is%20modeled.%20In%20Hill-type%20models%2C%20the%20modeling%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20is%20phenomenological%3B%20arbitrary%20mathematical%20functions%20are%20used%20to%20reproduce%20experimental%20observations%20relating%20muscle%20characteristics%20(such%20as%20excitation%2Factivation%2C%20muscle%20length%20and%20velocity)%20with%20the%20muscle%20force.%20In%20Huxley-type%20models%2C%20the%20modeling%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20is%20mechanistic%3B%20the%20mathematical%20functions%20used%20represent%20the%20hypothesized%20mechanisms%20for%20the%20cross-bridge%20dynamics%20(Tsianos%20and%20Loeb%2C%202013).%20Huxley-type%20models%20tend%20to%20produce%20more%20realistic%20results%20than%20Hill-type%20models%20for%20certain%20conditions%20but%20they%20have%20a%20higher%20computational%20demand.%20For%20this%20reason%2C%20Hill-type%20models%20are%20more%20often%20employed%20in%20musculoskeletal%20modeling%20and%20simulation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Hill-type%20muscle%20models%20are%20presented%20in%20several%20texts%20(e.g.%2C%20Erdermir%20et%20al.%202007%3B%20He%20et%20al.%2C%201991%3B%20McMahon%2C%201984%3B%20Nigg%20and%20Herzog%2C%202007%3B%20Robertson%20et%20al.%2C%202013%2C%20Thelen%2C%202003%3B%20Tsianos%20and%20Loeb%2C%202013%2C%20Winters%2C%201990%3B%20Zajac%2C%201989%3B%20Zatsiorsky%20and%20Prilutsky%2C%202012)%20and%20implemented%20in%20many%20software%20for%20modeling%20and%20simulation%20of%20the%20musculoskeletal%20dynamics%20of%20human%20movement%20(e.g.%2C%20the%20free%20and%20open%20source%20software%20%5BOpenSim%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fsimtk.org%2Fhome%2Fopensim)).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Next%2C%20let's%20see%20a%20brief%20overview%20of%20a%20Hill-type%20muscle%20model%20and%20a%20basic%20implementation%20in%20Python.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**The%20modeling%20story.**%20A%20Hill-type%20model%20is%20a%20compact%20way%20to%20represent%20the%20macroscopic%20behavior%20of%20a%20muscle-tendon%20actuator.%20It%20does%20not%20model%20every%20cross-bridge%20directly.%20Instead%2C%20it%20uses%20empirical%20functions%20that%20reproduce%20important%20observations%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20muscle%20can%20pull%20but%20not%20push%3B%0A%20%20%20%20-%20active%20force%20is%20largest%20near%20an%20optimal%20fiber%20length%3B%0A%20%20%20%20-%20passive%20force%20grows%20when%20muscle%20or%20tendon%20is%20stretched%3B%0A%20%20%20%20-%20shortening%20muscle%20produces%20less%20force%20than%20an%20isometric%20muscle%3B%0A%20%20%20%20-%20lengthening%20muscle%20can%20produce%20more%20force%20than%20an%20isometric%20muscle%3B%0A%20%20%20%20-%20activation%20cannot%20change%20instantaneously.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Hill-type%20muscle%20model%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Hill-type%20models%20are%20developed%20to%20reproduce%20the%20dependence%20of%20force%20with%20the%20length%20and%20velocity%20of%20the%20muscle-tendon%20unit%20and%20parameters%20are%20lumped%20and%20made%20dimensionless%20in%20order%20to%20represent%20different%20muscles%20with%20few%20changes%20in%20these%20parameters.%20A%20Hill-type%20model%20is%20complemented%20with%20the%20modeling%20of%20the%20activation%20dynamics%20(i.e.%2C%20the%20temporal%20pattern%20of%20muscle%20activation%20and%20deactivation%20as%20a%20function%20of%20the%20neural%20excitation)%20to%20produce%20more%20realistic%20results.%20As%20a%20result%2C%20the%20force%20generated%20will%20be%20a%20function%20of%20three%20factors%3A%20the%20length%20and%20velocity%20of%20the%20muscle-tendon%20unit%20and%20its%20activation%20level%20%24a%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20Hill-type%20muscle%20model%20has%20three%20components%20(see%20figure%20below)%3A%20two%20for%20the%20muscle%2C%20an%20active%20contractile%20element%20(CE)%20and%20a%20passive%20elastic%20element%20(PE)%20in%20parallel%20with%20the%20CE%2C%20and%20one%20component%20for%20the%20tendon%2C%20an%20elastic%20element%20(SE)%20in%20series%20with%20the%20muscle.%20In%20some%20variations%2C%20a%20damping%20component%20is%20added%20parallel%20to%20the%20CE%20as%20a%20fourth%20element.%20A%20%5Bpennation%20angle%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FMuscle_architecture)%20(angle%20of%20the%20pennate%20fibers%20with%20respect%20to%20the%20force-generating%20axis)%20is%20also%20included%20in%20the%20model.%20In%20a%20simpler%20approach%2C%20the%20muscle%20and%20tendon%20are%20assumed%20massless.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Fmuscle_hill.png%22%20width%3D400%20alt%3D%22Hill-type%20muscle%20model.%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%0A%20%20%20%20%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20A%20Hill-type%20muscle%20model%20with%20three%20components%3A%20two%20for%20the%20muscle%2C%20an%20active%20contractile%20element%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BCE%7D%24%2C%20and%20a%20passive%20elastic%20element%20in%20parallel%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BPE%7D%24%2C%20with%20the%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BCE%7D%24%2C%20and%20one%20component%20for%20the%20tendon%2C%20an%20elastic%20element%20in%20series%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BSE%7D%24%2C%20with%20the%20muscle.%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BL_%7BMT%7D%7D%24%3A%20muscle%E2%80%93tendon%20length%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BL_T%7D%24%3A%20tendon%20length%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BL_M%7D%24%3A%20muscle%20fiber%20length%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BF_T%7D%24%3A%20tendon%20force%2C%20%24%5Cmathsf%7BF_M%7D%24%3A%20muscle%20force%2C%20and%20%24%CE%B1%24%3A%20pennation%20angle.%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20now%20revise%20the%20models%20of%20a%20Hill-type%20muscle%20with%20three%20components%20and%20activation%20dynamics%20by%20two%20references%3A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20%5BThelen%20(2003)%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fsimtk-confluence.stanford.edu%3A8080%2Fdisplay%2FOpenSim%2FThelen%2B2003%2BMuscle%2BModel)%20with%20some%20of%20the%20adjustments%20described%20in%20Millard%20et%20al.%20(2013).%20Hereafter%2C%20Thelen2003Muscle%20or%20T03.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20%5BMcLean%2C%20Su%2C%20van%20den%20Bogert%20(2003)%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fpubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2F14986412).%20Hereafter%2C%20McLean2003Muscle%20or%20M03.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%201.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Which%20element%20produces%20active%20tensile%20force%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Which%20element%20accounts%20for%20passive%20force%20when%20the%20muscle%20is%20stretched%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20does%20a%20tendon%20belong%20in%20series%20with%20the%20muscle%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20If%20tendon%20is%20elastic%2C%20why%20might%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20change%20even%20when%20the%20whole%20muscle-tendon%20length%20is%20fixed%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20First%2C%20let's%20import%20the%20necessary%20Python%20libraries%20and%20customize%20the%20environment%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20'%25matplotlib%20notebook'%20command%20supported%20automatically%20in%20marimo%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib.pyplot%20as%20plt%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib%0A%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rcParams%5B%22lines.linewidth%22%5D%20%3D%202%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rcParams%5B%22font.size%22%5D%20%3D%2012%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rcParams%5B%22lines.markersize%22%5D%20%3D%204%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22axes%22%2C%20grid%3DTrue%2C%20labelsize%3D12%2C%20titlesize%3D13%2C%20ymargin%3D0.01)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22legend%22%2C%20numpoints%3D1%2C%20fontsize%3D10)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20np%2C%20plt%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Force-length%20relationship%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20a%20Hill-type%20model%2C%20the%20force%20a%20muscle%20can%20generate%20depends%20on%20its%20length%20due%20to%20two%20factors%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20active%20force%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20(CE)%2C%20which%20in%20turn%20depends%20on%20the%20spatial%20superposition%20of%20the%20actin%20and%20myosin%20molecules%20to%20form%20cross-bridges%20at%20the%20sarcomere.%20A%20maximum%20number%20of%20cross-bridges%20will%20be%20formed%20at%20an%20optimal%20fiber%20length%2C%20generating%20a%20maximum%20force.%20When%20a%20fiber%20is%20too%20stretched%20or%20too%20shortened%2C%20fewer%20cross-bridges%20will%20be%20formed%2C%20decreasing%20the%20force%20generated.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20passive%20and%20parallel%20elastic%20element%20(PE)%2C%20which%20behaves%20as%20a%20nonlinear%20spring%20where%20no%20force%20is%20generated%20below%20a%20certain%20length%20(the%20slack%20length)%20and%20force%20increases%20with%20the%20muscle%20elongation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20running%20the%20force-length%20plots**%2C%20predict%20where%20total%20force%20can%20exceed%20the%20maximum%20active%20isometric%20force.%20Is%20that%20because%20the%20active%20curve%20is%20larger%2C%20because%20the%20passive%20curve%20has%20turned%20on%2C%20or%20both%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Chapter%202%20bridge%20problem.**%20In%20a%20separate%20scratch%20cell%20or%20notebook%2C%20design%20a%20normalized%20active%20force-length%20function%20inspired%20by%20Yamaguchi's%20qualitative%20description%3A%20near%20zero%20at%20very%20short%20and%20very%20long%20fiber%20lengths%2C%20maximal%20near%20optimal%20fiber%20length%2C%20and%20scaled%20by%20activation.%20Do%20not%20replace%20the%20Thelen%20or%20McLean%20curves%20here%3B%20use%20them%20as%20comparison%20targets.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%23%20Force-length%20relationship%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Thelen2003Muscle%20represented%20the%20normalized%20force-length%20relationship%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20by%20a%20Gaussian%20function%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%3D%20exp%5Cleft%5B-(%5Cbar%7BL%7D_M-1)%5E2%2F%5Cgamma%5Cright%5D%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24%5Cgamma%24%20is%20a%20shape%20factor%20and%20%24%5Cbar%7BL%7D_M%24%20is%20the%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20normalized%20by%20the%20optimal%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20at%20which%20maximal%20force%20can%20be%20produced%2C%20%24L_%7BMopt%7D%24%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%5Cbar%7BL%7D_M%3D%5Cfrac%7BL_M%7D%7BL_%7BMopt%7D%7D%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Thelen2003Muscle%20adopted%20%24%5Cgamma%3D0.45%24.%20The%20actual%20force%20produced%20is%20obtained%20multiplying%20%24%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%24%20by%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20muscle%20force%2C%20%24F_%7BM0%7D%24.%20Thelen2003Muscle%20assumed%20that%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20muscle%20forces%20for%20old%20adults%20were%2030%25%20lower%20than%20those%20used%20for%20young%20adults.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20McLean2003Muscle%20represented%20the%20force-length%20relationship%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20(not%20normalized)%20as%20a%20fu 20strain%20above%20which%20the%20tendon%20exhibits%20linear%20behavior%2C%20%24k_%7BTtoe%7D%24%20is%20an%20exponential%20shape%20factor%2C%20and%20%24k_%7BTlin%7D%24%20is%20a%20linear%20scale%20factor.%20The%20parameters%20are%20chosen%20such%20that%20the%20tendon%20elongation%20at%20the%20normalized%20maximal%20isometric%20force%20of%20the%20muscle%20is%204%25%20of%20the%20tendon%20length%20(%24%5Cepsilon_%7BT0%7D%3D0.04%24).%0A%20%20%20%20Thelen2003Muscle%20adopted%20%24k_%7BTtoe%7D%3D3%24%20and%20the%20transition%20from%20nonlinear%20to%20linear%20behavior%20occurs%20for%20normalized%20tendon%20forces%20greater%20than%20%24%5Cbar%7BF%7D_%7BTtoe%7D%3D0.33%24.%20For%20continuity%20of%20slopes%20at%20the%20transition%2C%20%24%5Cepsilon_%7BTtoe%7D%3D0.609%5Cepsilon_%7BT0%7D%24%20and%20%24k_%7BTlin%7D%3D1.712%2F%5Cepsilon_%7BT0%7D%24.%20The%20actual%20force%20produced%20is%20obtained%20multiplying%20%24%5Cbar%7BF%7D_%7BSE%7D%24%20by%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20muscle%20force%2C%20%24F_%7BM0%7D%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20McLean2003Muscle%20represented%20the%20tendon%20force%20(not%20normalized)%20of%20the%20series%20element%20as%20a%20function%20of%20the%20tendon%20length%20(not%20normalized)%20by%20the%20same%20quadratic%20function%20used%20for%20the%20force%20of%20the%20muscle%20passive%20element%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20F_%7BSE%7D(L_T)%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5C%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%200%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20L_T%20%5Cleq%20L_%7BTslack%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20k_T(L_T%20-%20L_%7BTslack%7D)%5E2%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20L_T%20%3E%20L_%7BTslack%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%5Cright.%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24k_T%24%20is%20the%20tendon%20stiffness.%20The%20stiffness%20parameter%20%24k_T%24%20is%20chosen%20such%20that%20the%20tendon%20elongation%20is%204%25%20at%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20force%2C%20%24k_T%3D(1%2F%5Cepsilon_%7BT0%7D)%5E2%3D625%24%20for%20%24F_%7BM0%7D%3D1%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Tendon%20prompt.**%20Chapter%202%20emphasizes%20that%20tendon%20elasticity%20can%20change%20the%20relationship%20between%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20and%20whole%20muscle-tendon%20length.%20Before%20plotting%20the%20tendon%20curves%2C%20predict%20which%20model%20is%20initially%20more%20compliant%20and%20which%20becomes%20stiffer%20at%20larger%20stretch.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Chapter%202%20bridge%20problem.**%20Implement%20a%20tendon%20force-strain%20curve%20with%20a%20toe%20region%20followed%20by%20a%20linear%20region%20in%20a%20separate%20scratch%20cell%20or%20notebook.%20Then%20formulate%2C%20but%20do%20not%20solve%20here%2C%20the%20fixed-length%20muscle-tendon%20equilibrium%20problem%20where%20tendon%20force%20must%20equal%20muscle%20force.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20corresponding%20Python%20functions%20are%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20def%20fselt_T03(lt%3D1%2C%20ltslack%3D1%2C%20epst0%3D0.04%2C%20kttoe%3D3)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Thelen%20(2003)%20force-length%20relationship%20of%20tendon%20as%20function%20of%20tendon%20length.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Parameters%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20----------%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20lt%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20normalized%20tendon%20length%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ltslack%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20normalized%20tendon%20slack%20length%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20epst0%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D0.04)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20tendon%20strain%20at%20the%20maximal%20isometric%20muscle%20force%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20kttoe%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D3)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20linear%20scale%20factor%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20Returns%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20-------%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fse%20%20%3A%20float%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20normalized%20force%20of%20the%20tendon%20series%20element%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20epst%20%3D%20(lt%20-%20ltslack)%20%2F%20ltslack%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fttoe%20%3D%200.33%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%20values%20from%20OpenSim%20Thelen2003Muscle%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20epsttoe%20%3D%200.99%20*%20epst0%20*%20np.e**3%20%2F%20(1.66%20*%20np.e**3%20-%200.67)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ktlin%20%3D%200.67%20%2F%20(epst0%20-%20epsttoe)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%23%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20if%20epst%20%3C%3D%200%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fse%20%3D%200%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20elif%20epst%20%3C%3D%20epsttoe%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fse%20%3D%20fttoe%20%2F%20(np.exp(kttoe)%20-%201)%20*%20(np.exp(kttoe%20*%20epst%20%2F%20epsttoe)%20-%201)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20else%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20fse%20%3D%20ktlin%20*%20(epst%20-%20epsttoe)%20%2B%20fttoe%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20return%20fse%0A%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(fselt_T03%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20fselt_M03(lt%2C%20ltslack%3D1%2C%20fm0%3D1%2C%20epst0%3D0.04)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22McLean%20(2003)%20force-length%20relationship%20of%20tendon%20as%20function%20of%20tendon%20length.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Parameters%0A%20%20%20%20----------%0A%20%20%20%20lt%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20tendon%20length%0A%20%20%20%20ltslack%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20tendon%20slack%20length%0A%20%20%20%20fm0%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20maximum%20isometric%20muscle%20force%0A%20%20%20%20epst0%20%20%3A%20float%2C%20optional%20(default%3D0.04)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20tendon%20strain%20at%20the%20maximal%20isometric%20muscle%20force%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Returns%0A%20%20%20%20-------%0A%20%20%20%20fse%20%20%3A%20float%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20force%20of%2 20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%202%20%E2%80%94%20Balance%20a%20pennated%20fiber.**%20A%20fiber%20produces%20600%20N%20at%20a%20pennation%20angle%20of%2030%C2%B0.%20What%20tendon%20force%20follows%20from%20static%20force%20balance%2C%20ignoring%20tendon%20inertia%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Solution%20to%20Exercise%202'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%24F_T%3DF_M%5Ccos%5Calpha%3D600%5Ccos30%5E%5Ccirc%5Capprox519.6%24%20N.%20Fiber%20force%20and%20tendon%20force%20are%20equal%20only%20at%20zero%20pennation%20in%20this%20simple%20model.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Force-velocity%20relationship%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20force-velocity%20relation%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20for%20shortening%20(concentric%20activation)%20is%20based%20on%20the%20well%20known%20Hill's%20equation%20of%20a%20hyperbola%20describing%20that%20the%20product%20between%20force%20%24F%24%20and%20velocity%20%24V%24%20of%20the%20contractile%20element%20is%20constant%20(Winters%2C%201990%3B%20Winters%2C%201995)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20(F%2Ba')(V%2Bb')%20%3D%20(F_%7B0%7D%2Ba')b'%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24a'%24%2C%20%24b'%24%2C%20and%20%24F_%7B0%7D%24%20are%20constants.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20can%20rewrite%20the%20equation%20above%20with%20constants%20more%20meaningful%20to%20our%20modeling%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20(F_%7BM%7D%2BA_f%20F_%7BMlen%7D)(V_M%2BA_f%20V_%7BMmax%7D)%20%3D%20A_f%20F_%7BMlen%7DV_%7BMmax%7D(1%2BA_f)%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24F_%7BM%7D%24%20and%20%24V_M%24%20are%20the%20contractile%20element%20force%20and%20velocity%2C%20respectively%2C%20and%20the%20three%20constants%20are%3A%20%24V_%7BMmax%7D%24%2C%20the%20maximum%20unloaded%20velocity%20(when%20%24F_%7BM%7D%3D0%24)%2C%20%24F_%7BMlen%7D%24%2C%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20force%20(when%20%24V_M%3D0%24)%2C%20and%20%24A_f%24%2C%20a%20shape%20factor%20which%20specifies%20the%20concavity%20of%20the%20hyperbola.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Based%20on%20the%20equation%20above%20for%20the%20shortening%20phase%20and%20in%20Winters%20(1990%2C%201995)%20for%20the%20lengthening%20phase%2C%20Thelen2003Muscle%20employed%20the%20following%20force-velocity%20equation%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20V_M%20%3D%20(0.25%2B0.75a)%5C%2CV_%7BMmax%7D%5Cfrac%7B%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M-a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%7D%7Bb%7D%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20b%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5C%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%2B%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M%2FA_f%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M%20%5Cleq%20a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(shortening)%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7B(2%2B2%2FA_f)(a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D%20-%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M)%7D%7B%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D-1%7D%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20%5Cbar%7BF%7D_M%20%3E%20a%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bl%2CCE%7D%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(lengthening)%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%5Cright.%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24a%24%20is%20the%20activation%20level%20and%20%24%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D%24%20is%20a%20constant%20for%20the%20maximum%20force%20generated%20at%20the%20lengthening%20phase%20(normalized%20by%20the%20maximum%20isometric%20force).%0A%20%20%20%20Thelen2003Muscle%20adopted%20%24A_f%3D0.25%24%2C%20%24V_%7BMmax%7D%3D10L_%7BMopt%7D%2Fs%24%2C%20%24%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D%3D1.4%24%20for%20young%20adults%20(%24V_%7BMmax%7D%3D8L_%7BMopt%7D%2Fs%24%20and%20%24%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D%3D1.8%24%20for%20old%20adults).%20Note%20that%20the%20dependences%20of%20the%20force%20with%20the%20activation%20level%20and%20with%20the%20muscle%20length%20are%20already%20incorporated%20in%20the%20expression%20above.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20McLean2013Muscle%20employed%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7Bv%2CCE%7D%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5C%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Clambda(a)V_%7BMmax%7D%20%2B%20V_M%7D%7B%5Clambda(a)V_%7BMmax%7D%20-%20V_M%2FA_f%7D%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20V_M%20%5Cleq%200%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(shortening)%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7DV_M%20%2B%20d_1%7D%7BV_M%20%2B%20d_1%7D%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%200%20%3C%20V_M%20%5Cleq%20%5Cgamma%20d_1%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(slow%20lengthening)%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d_3%20%2B%20d_2V_M%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20V_M%20%3E%20%5Cgamma%20d_1%20%26%20%5Ctext%7B(fast%20lengthening)%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%5Cright.%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Clambda(a)%20%3D%201-e%5E%7B-3.82a%7D%20%2B%20a%5C%3Ae%5E%7B-3.82%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d_1%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7BV_%7BMmax%7DA_f(%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D-1)%7D%7BS(A_f%2B1)%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d_2%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7BS(A_f%2B1)%7D%7BV_%7BMmax%7DA_f(%5Cgamma%2B1)%5E2%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20d_3%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B(%5Cbar%7Bf%7D_%7BMlen%7D-1)%5Cgamma%5E2%7D%7B(%5Cgamma%2B1)%5E2%7D%20%2B%201%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24%5Clambda(a)%24%20is%20a%20scaling%20factor%20to%20account%20for%20the%20influence%20of%20the%20activation%20level%20%24a%24%20on%20the%20force-velocity%20relationship%2C%20% 2C%20the%20activation%20dynamics%20is%20generally%20represented%20as%20a%20first-order%20ODE.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Activation%20is%20a%20state%20variable%2C%20not%20an%20algebraic%20copy%20of%20excitation.%20In%20Yamaguchi's%20Chapter%202%20framing%2C%20the%20control%20input%20is%20a%20mathematical%20signal%20between%200%20and%201%2C%20while%20activation%20describes%20the%20delayed%20muscle%20state%20that%20results%20from%20that%20signal.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20running%20the%20activation%20plots**%2C%20predict%20how%20activation%20should%20differ%20from%20excitation%20when%20the%20excitation%20pulse%20turns%20on%20and%20when%20it%20turns%20off.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Chapter%202%20bridge%20problem.**%20Implement%20the%20He-Zajac-Levine%20bilinear%20activation%20model%20in%20a%20separate%20scratch%20cell%20or%20notebook.%20Test%20three%20cases%3A%20a%20rise%20from%20rest%2C%20a%20decay%20from%20an%20active%20state%2C%20and%20an%20intermediate%20control%20value%20such%20as%20%5C(c(t)%3D0.6%5C).%20Compare%20the%20result%20with%20the%20Thelen%20and%20McLean%20activation%20curves%20below%20without%20replacing%20them.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Thelen2003Muscle%20employed%20the%20following%20first-order%20%5Bordinary%20differential%20equation%20(ODE)%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FOrdinary_differential_equation)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Da%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bu-a%7D%7B%5Ctau(a%2C%20u)%7D%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20with%20a%20lower%20activation%20bound%20to%20both%20activation%20and%20excitation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24u%24%20and%20%24a%24%20are%20the%20muscle%20excitation%20and%20activation%2C%20respectively%20(both%20are%20function%20of%20time)%2C%20and%20%24%5Ctau%24%20is%20a%20variable%20time%20constant%20to%20represent%20the%20activation%20and%20deactivation%20times%2C%20given%20by%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Ctau(a%2C%20u)%20%3D%20%5Cleft%5C%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20t_%7Bact%7D(0.5%2B1.5a)%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20u%20%3E%20a%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%5Cfrac%7Bt_%7Bdeact%7D%7D%7B(0.5%2B1.5a)%7D%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctext%7Bif%7D%20%5Cquad%20u%20%5Cleq%20a%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%20%5Cright.%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Thelen2003Muscle%20adopted%20activation%2C%20%24t_%7Bact%7D%24%2C%20and%20deactivation%2C%20%24t_%7Bdeact%7D%24%2C%20time%20constants%20for%20young%20adults%20equal%20to%2015%20and%2050%20ms%2C%20respectively%20(for%20old%20adults%2C%20Thelen2003Muscle%20adopted%2015%20and%2060%20ms%2C%20respectively).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20McLean2003Muscle%20expressed%20the%20activation%20dynamics%20as%20the%20following%20first-order%20ODE%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Da%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20(u%20-%20a)(c_1u%20%2B%20c_2)%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20with%20a%20lower%20activation%20bound%20to%20both%20activation%20and%20excitation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24c_1%20%2B%20c_2%24%20is%20the%20activation%20rate%20constant%20(when%20%24u%20%3D%201%24)%2C%20the%20inverse%20of%20%24t_%7Bact%7D%24%2C%20and%20%24c_2%24%20is%20the%20deactivation%20rate%20constant%20(when%20%24u%20%3D%200%24)%2C%20the%20inverse%20of%20%24t_%7Bdeact%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20McLean2003Muscle%20adopted%20%24c_1%3D3.3%20s%5E%7B-1%7D%24%20and%20%24c_2%3D16.7%20s%5E%7B-1%7D%24%2C%20resulting%20in%20time%20constants%20of%2050%20ms%20and%2060%20ms%20for%20activation%20and%20deactivation%2C%20respectively.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20Python%2C%20the%20numeric%20first-order%20ODE%20for%20the%20activation%20dynamics%20presented%20in%20Thelen2003Muscle%20can%20be%20expressed%20as%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20actdyn_T03(t%2C%20a%2C%20t_act%2C%20t_deact%2C%20u_max%2C%20u_min%2C%20t0%3D0.1%2C%20t1%3D0.4)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Thelen%20(2003)%20activation%20dynamics%2C%20the%20derivative%20of%20%60a%60%20at%20%60t%60.%0A%0A%20%20% 22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Limitations%20of%20Hill-type%20muscle%20models%0A%0A%20%20%20%20As%20with%20any%20modeling%2C%20Hill-type%20muscle%20models%20are%20a%20simplification%20of%20the%20reality.%20For%20instance%2C%20a%20typical%20Hill-type%20muscle%20model%20(as%20implemented%20here)%20does%20not%20capture%20time-dependent%20muscle%20behavior%2C%20such%20as%20force%20depression%20after%20quick%20muscle%20shortening%2C%20force%20enhancement%20after%20quick%20muscle%20lengthening%2C%20viscoelastic%20%20properties%20(creep%20and%20relaxation)%2C%20and%20muscle%20fatigue%20(Zatsiorsky%20and%20Prilutsky%2C%202012).%20There%20are%20enhanced%20models%20that%20capture%20these%20properties%20but%20it%20seems%20their%20complexity%20are%20not%20worthy%20for%20the%20most%20common%20applications%20of%20human%20movement%20simulation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Checkpoint%20questions.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Why%20is%20activation%20a%20state%20variable%20rather%20than%20an%20algebraic%20copy%20of%20excitation%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Which%20part%20of%20the%20model%20explains%20force%20at%20zero%20activation%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20does%20shortening%20velocity%20reduce%20active%20force%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Why%20can%20lengthening%20velocity%20increase%20active%20force%3F%0A%20%20%20%205.%20In%20a%20fixed-length%20muscle-tendon%20unit%2C%20why%20can%20muscle%20fiber%20length%20still%20change%20after%20activation%20changes%3F%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Which%20assumptions%20in%20this%20notebook%20would%20you%20remove%20first%20for%20a%20more%20realistic%20simulation%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Answers%20to%20the%20earlier%20muscle-model%20checkpoints'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Activation%20evolves%20over%20time%20rather%20than%20copying%20excitation%20instantly.%202.%20Passive%20elastic%20force.%203.%20Shortening%20reduces%20force%20through%20the%20active%20force%E2%80%93velocity%20relation.%204.%20The%20modeled%20eccentric%20branch%20permits%20larger%20active%20force%20up%20to%20its%20limit.%205.%20Fiber%20and%20tendon%20lengths%20exchange%2C%20with%20pennation%20coupling%20their%20projections.%206.%20The%20first%20assumption%20to%20relax%20depends%20on%20the%20task%3A%20fatigue%20for%20repeated%20work%2C%20history%20dependence%20for%20stretch%E2%80%93shorten%20behavior%2C%20or%20geometry%2Fcompliance%20for%20architectural%20effects.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Checkpoint%20questions%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Which%20force%20branches%20remain%20when%20activation%20is%20zero%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20How%20is%20power%20affected%20by%20your%20shortening-velocity%20sign%20convention%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20can%20tendon%20force%20change%20while%20total%20musculotendon%20length%20stays%20fixed%3F%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Which%20conclusions%20depend%20on%20the%20chosen%20Hill-model%20parameterization%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Checkpoint%20answers'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Passive%20muscle%20and%20tendon%20forces%20can%20remain%20if%20stretched.%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Fiber%20power%20uses%20force%20times%20signed%20lengthening%20velocity%3B%20positive%20delivered%20shortening%20power%20uses%20the%20opposite%20sign.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Fiber%20and%20tendon%20lengths%20can%20exchange%20while%20their%20total%20projected%20length%20remains%20fixed.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Exact%20curve%20shapes%2C%20eccentric%20limits%2C%20time%20constants%2C%20and%20quantitative%20force%20predictions.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Problems%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20results%20presented%20in%20this%20text%20depend%20on%20the%20parameters%20used%20in%20the%20model.%20These%20parameters%20may%20vary%20because%20of%20different%20properties%20of%20the%20muscle%20and%20tendon%20but%20also%20because%20different%20mathematical%20functions%20may%20be%20used.%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a.%20Change%20some%20of%20the%20parameters%20and%20reproduce%20the%20plots%20shown%20here%20and%20discuss%20these%20results%20(e.g.%2C%20use%20the%20parameters%20for%20different%20muscles%20from%20OpenSim%20or%20the%20data%20from%20%5Bhttp%3A%2F%2Fisbweb.org%2Fdata%2Fdelp%2F%5D(http%3A%2F%2Fisbweb.org%2Fdata%2Fdelp%2F)).%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b.%20Select%20another%20reference%20(e.g.%2C%20Anderson%2C%202007)%20about%20muscle%20modeling%20that%20uses%20different%20mathematical%20functions%20and%20repeat%20the%20previous%20item.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Activation%20rise%20and%20decay.%20Implement%20the%20He-Zajac-Levine%20bilinear%20activation%20model%20from%20Chapter%202%20as%20a%20new%20function%20in%20a%20separate%20scratch%20cell%20or%20notebook.%20Simulate%20%5C(c(t)%3D1%5C)%2C%20%5C(c(t)%3D0.6%5C)%2C%20and%20%5C(c(t)%3D0%5C).%20Explain%20why%20activation%20and%20deactivation%20do%20not%20use%20the%20same%20time%20constant.%20Do%20not%20replace%20the%20Thelen%20or%20McLean%20activation%20plots%20above.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Activation%20function%20tests.%20Write%20unit-style%20checks%20for%20your%20activation%20function%3A%20%5C(a(t)%5C)%20should%20stay%20between%200%20and%201%2C%20%5C(c%3D1%5C)%20should%20rise%20quickly%20from%20rest%2C%20and%20%5C(c%3D0%5C)%20should%20decay%20from%20an%20active%20state.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20Active%20force-length%20implementation.%20Implement%20a%20normalized%20active%20force-length%20function%20that%20is%20zero%20or%20near%20zero%20near%20%5C(0.5l_0%5EM%5C)%20and%20%5C(1.5l_0%5EM%5C)%2C%20maximal%20at%20%5C(l_0%5EM%5C)%2C%20and%20scaled%20by%20activation.%20Compare%20a%20parabolic%2C%20cosine%2C%20or%20piecewise-linear%20version%20with%20the%20Thelen%20and%20McLean%20curves%20shown%20above.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Passive%20force-length%20implementation.%20Implement%20an%20exponential%20passive%20force-length%20function.%20Choose%20parameters%20so%20passive%20force%20at%20a%20stretched%20fiber%20length%20is%2025%25%2C%2050%25%2C%20and%20100%25%20of%20%5C(F_0%5EM%5C).%20How%20does%20this%20change%20total%20force%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Hill%20force-velocity%20implementation.%20Implement%20the%20shortening%20branch%20of%20Hill's%20equation%20and%20plot%20force%20versus%20normalized%20shortening%20velocity.%20Then%20compute%20the%20velocity%20at%20which%20positive%20shortening%20power%20is%20maximal.%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20Lengthening%20branch%20design.%20Add%20an%20eccentric%20branch%20that%20approaches%20a%20finite%20force%20limit.%20Explain%20why%20a%20force%20limit%20is%20more%20realistic%20than%20a%20line%20that%20grows%20forever.%0A%0A%20%20%20%208.%20Full%20muscle%20force.%20Combine%20activation%2C%20active%20length%20dependence%2C%20passive%20length%20dependence%2C%20and%20velocity%20dependence%20into%20one%20force%20function.%20Plot%20force%20as%20a%20surface%20over%20length%20and%20velocity%20for%20%5C(a%3D0.25%5C)%2C%20%5C(0.5%5C)%2C%20and%20%5C(1.0%5C).%0A%0A%20%20%20%209.%20Tendon%20equilibrium.%20For%20a%20fixed%20musculotendon%20length%2C%20solve%20for%20the%20fiber%20length%20where%20muscle%20force%20and%20tendon%20force%20are%20equal.%20Compare%20a%20stiff%20tendon%20with%20a%20compliant%20tendon.%0A%0A%20%20%20%2010.%20Energy%20storage.%20Use%20tendon%20force%20and%20tendon%20velocity%20to%20estimate%20tendon%20power.%20When%20is%20tendon%20storing%20energy%2C%20and%20when%20is%20it%20returning%20energy%3F%0
